analysis:
In his Independence Day address on 15 August 2026, the Prime Minister said that from 2004 to 2014 there were fewer than 350 universities, and that 'nearly 650 new universities' had been added in the following 10-12 years, taking the figure toward 1,000.

Government education statistics give different levels. A PIB release of April 2023 stated that the number of universities rose from 723 in 2014 to 1,113 in 2023, an increase of 390. A PIB document published in August 2026, citing the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) 2023-24, recorded university-level institutions rising from 760 in 2014-15 to 1,289 in 2023-24, an increase of about 529.

Both official series indicate a substantial expansion, but the stated addition of 'nearly 650' universities and the 'fewer than 350' starting point do not correspond to the AISHE counts.
notes: The speech was in Hindi; the quoted English is the PTI rendering. Different AISHE editions and different definitions of 'university' (UGC-recognised universities vs AISHE university-level institutions, which include deemed and private universities) produce different totals, so the claim is marked 'misleading' rather than 'false'. This is distinct from the excluded modi-2020-iit-iim-iiit-numbers-before-2014 claim, which concerned IITs/IIMs/IIITs. The PTI report's transcription of the medical-colleges sentence is internally inconsistent ('400 medical seats... 850 medical seats') and is not used here.
